findings.detail: Identity validation requires a field value in the fact statement, but not in its supporting quotation. A drivetrain fact stating AWD can therefore be bound to an unrelated quotation from a source whose declared scope matches the intake. Matching scope labels alone do not establish that the source supports the field.
findings.required_fix: Bind each identity value to directly supporting source text and its exact vehicle context; add active-article tests for unrelated quotations and mismatched identity values.

findings.detail: The standard gate relies on a limited expression and skips classification checks for facts labeled editorial_method. A regulation cited without a recognized term, or mislabeled as an editorial method, can bypass current-version and primary-source requirements.
findings.required_fix: Classify regulatory and standards claims independently of the supplied kind flag, fail closed when classification is uncertain, and test alternate citation formats and mislabeled mandatory claims.

findings.detail: CROSS_CHECKED requires two parent organizations but does not restrict the sources to tiers permitted for the fact. For the Q05 intake, Autohome and YooJia are declared T3; the gate can therefore accept their agreement as support for a core vehicle specification even though the repository limits T3 to background, process and case-study use.
findings.required_fix: Enforce fact-specific source-tier eligibility. Reclassify structured sources only after validating their actual publisher and content, and test that two T3 sources cannot establish a key vehicle specification.

findings.detail: The engine never sets a durable WRITING_LOCK while writing. It requires writing_locked=false and compares only its cached research checkpoint, so concurrent Research changes outside that immutable checkpoint are not signaled through UPDATE_REQUIRED or RESEARCH_CHANGED_AFTER_WRITING_STARTED.
findings.required_fix: Implement durable per-article lock and update signaling, re-read the current versioned Research handoff before completion, and test a Research change during writing.

findings.detail: The account-check job exposes the project key to code selected by AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA without the protected permit and workflow-lease preauthorization used by execute. The application-level SHA check runs only after that selected code has received the key; the protected environment review does not itself bind the code to a reviewed account-check implementation.
findings.required_fix: Run account checks from an independently pinned implementation, or validate a protected, code-bound account-check permit before exposing the project key.

findings.detail: When a target evidence checkpoint already exists, restore validates its declarations and internal hashes but does not compare its raw hashes, retrieval times or target hash with the approved origin transfer. It can then produce a transfer receipt associating cached evidence with an origin it did not verify against that cache.
findings.required_fix: Bind every required transfer to the approved origin and expected target, and verify raw hashes, retrieval times, source declarations and target digest even when the target checkpoint already exists.

cloud-pilot-manual.yml.content:
name: AutoBridge multilingual API pilot
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      mode:
        description: Offline inspection or separately approved real execution
        type: choice
        options: [preflight, account-check, audit, execute]
        default: preflight
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: autobridge-entire-real-pilot-program
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  trusted:
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    uses: xysjou/AutoBridge-Content-Pipeline/.github/workflows/cloud-pilot-trusted.yml@a418353233e0a66a3385897a8845857fc09d2d26
    with:
      mode: ${{ inputs.mode }}
    secrets:
      OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
      AUTOBRIDGE_CONTROL_COMMIT: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_CONTROL_COMMIT }}
      AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256 }}

cloud-pilot-trusted.yml.content:
name: AutoBridge pinned protected runtime
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      mode:
        type: string
        required: true
    secrets:
      OPENAI_API_KEY:
        required: true
      AUTOBRIDGE_CONTROL_COMMIT:
        required: true
      AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256:
        required: true
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  inspect:
    if: inputs.mode == 'preflight'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
        with:
          ref: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - run: python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual preflight
  account-check:
    if: >-
      inputs.mode == 'account-check' &&
      vars.AUTOBRIDGE_ACCOUNT_CHECK_ENABLED == 'true' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/integration/work-cloud-pilot-m1-20261102'
    environment: autobridge-pilot
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
        with:
          ref: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA }}
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Inspect only the two configured model metadata endpoints
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_ACCOUNT_CHECK_APPROVED: 'true'
        run: python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual account-check
  execute:
    if: >-
      (inputs.mode == 'execute' || inputs.mode == 'audit') &&
      vars.AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_ENABLED == 'true' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/integration/work-cloud-pilot-m1-20261102'
    environment: autobridge-pilot
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262
        with:
          ref: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA }}
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Fetch reviewed control documents from a separate immutable commit
        env:
          AUTOBRIDGE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVAL_COMMIT: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_CONTROL_COMMIT }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA: ${{ vars.AUTOBRIDGE_APPROVED_CODE_SHA }}
        run: python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual.control
      - name: Validate exact run and workflow lease before exposing the project key
        env:
          AUTOBRIDGE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256 }}
        run: >-
          python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual preauthorize
          --plan "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-plan.json"
          --prices "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-prices.json"
          --permit "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-permit.json"
      - name: Execute approved phase with the existing whole-program budget
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256: ${{ secrets.AUTOBRIDGE_LIVE_APPROVAL_SHA256 }}
          APPROVED_RUN_MODE: ${{ inputs.mode }}
        run: >-
          python3 -m cloud_pilot.multilingual "$APPROVED_RUN_MODE"
          --plan "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-plan.json"
          --prices "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-prices.json"
          --permit "$RUNNER_TEMP/autobridge-approved/approved-permit.json"

articles.reason: The supplied full texts show the reserve is a 2024 China-market PHEV reference, while this proposal concerns a 2026 BEV and a specific shortlist decision; that is a meaningful year/powertrain distinction, not proof that all Q05 pages are unique. The RHD guide only mentions NEVO Q05 as a reported Thailand RHD prospect and focuses on factory-RHD verification, not evaluating this exact BEV as an urban sourcing candidate. However, the indexed Southeast Asia SUV shortlist and new-versus-used EV guide may address overlapping recommendation or buying decisions, and their full texts are needed to confirm whether Q05 is covered or the intent is already served.

The Aumark and Tianjin KR pages focus on vehicle configuration, chassis/upfit separation and buyer verification; the fleet guide discusses general tender-grade acceptance criteria. This proposal instead asks buyers and suppliers to agree on a pre-shipment acceptance demonstration and its evidence: VIN/equipment identity, cargo and ambient conditions, sensor records, door-opening pattern, power modes and responsibility boundaries. That is a distinct acceptance decision, provided the article stays focused on test protocol, records and sign-off rather than repeating model specifications or general reefer shopping advice.
